notes: TWO BLOCKS FOR FIVE TOP-LEVEL BANDS, and the other three are accounted for below rather than
left out. The page draws, in order: .crumbs, header.hero#contact-form, section#reach,
section#visit, section#faq, <FinalBand>. #visit and #faq are the two blocks; the rest is
unguarded template markup, and the split is deliberate on each one.
THE PAGE HAS THREE `sections` ROWS — reach, visit, faq — verified against the live endpoint on
2026-08-29. Two are claimed by the blocks above; `reach` is claimed by nothing and is listed
under `exempt.sections`, WITHOUT the usual freeze warning, because its band is not migrating:
it stays in the template and keeps reading the row live. `faqs`, `cards`, `images`,
`process_steps` and `toc_links` all come back null, so there is nothing else to claim.
BAND VOCABULARY IS INVERTED ON THIS SHEET, as it is on the pilot and on the hubs.
`.section.alt` is CHARCOAL (contact.css:162) and `.section.dark` is SAGE-PALE (contact.css:169).
Both `band` values below are resolved from those rules, not from the class name.
NO RAIL ON THIS ROUTE. There is no `.toc` nav in the template and `pageFields.tocLinks` is null,
so `nav_label` resolves blank on both blocks — which is the documented way a band stays out of a
rail — and the template carries no derivedTocLinks loop.
#reach IS THE ONE BAND THAT COULD LOOK LIKE AN OMISSION AND IS NOT. Its four .contact-card
anchors carry FontAwesome icons, an <ArrowBadge>, and — the decisive part — three of the four
card TITLES are site data: card 2 prints `phoneLabel` and card 4 prints `emailAddress`
(contact/index.astro:263-291 in the pre-migration file, :258-283 now). Storing those as literal
card rows would give this one page its own copy of the practice's phone number and email, which
is exactly what block_cta_fields()' href policy exists to prevent, and a `code_section` cannot
help either: it would freeze the eyebrow, heading and body that `sections.reach` feeds live
today. So the band stays template markup, unguarded, editable, and in place.
THAT IS ORDER-SAFE BECAUSE #reach LEADS. It sits ABOVE the whole block run, and PageBlocks is
mounted at #visit's position, so DOM order is reproduced exactly. This is the mirror image of
the general-dentistry `.closing` case (an unguarded band that is safe because it TRAILS the
run) and the opposite of the LocalTrust fault (a band left out of the list that should have
been in it, which came out at the bottom of the page). Neither risk applies while #reach is the
only leading band and #faq is the last block.
THE ON-PAGE TYPEFORM IS NOT A BAND. It lives inside header.hero (id `#contact-form`,
contact/index.astro:222-250) beside the hero copy, not in a section of its own, so /contact/
needs no form `code_section` — the hero is chrome and is never a block (spec 7). The four
.contact-card links and <FinalBand> both point at `#contact-form`, and the hero keeps emitting
that id on both branches.

blocks.band_evidence: contact/index.astro:288 <section class="section alt" id="visit"> — contact.css:162 — .contact .section.alt { background: var(--charcoal-green); color: #fff } with --charcoal-green aliased to --vs-charcoal-green at contact.css:20. `.alt` is the DARK one on this sheet and `.dark` is sage-pale (contact.css:169); reading the class name instead of the rule would put sage-pale here.

eyebrow.from_template: contact/index.astro:292 Visit our practice. The CMS row `sections.visit.eyebrow` is NULL on the live endpoint (verified 2026-08-29), so this word only exists in the template; leaving the field blank would delete it from the band.

aria_label.from_template: contact/index.astro:288 aria-label="Visit our practice" on the <section>. Same string as the eyebrow and a DIFFERENT job: this one is the landmark name a screen reader announces, and /our-office/ ships "Visit our office" for the same band — which is why the layout has the field at all. Blank must emit no attribute; "" strips the landmark name instead of falling back to the heading.

blocks.no_cta_fields_note: This layout has no cta fields, and the two buttons in the band are not missing. "Get Directions" and "Call {phone}" resolve from src/data/contact.ts INSIDE MapVisitBlock, as do the street, city, state, zip, email, the officeHours table and the map embed. A per-band copy of any of them is a per-band chance to publish a stale phone number — the href policy.
blocks.reveal_attributes_note: The <section> itself carries NO data-vs-reveal-batch on this band — contact/index.astro:288 has none. The reveal hooks sit one level in: data-vs-reveal-batch on .location-copy (:290) and data-vs-reveal on .location-map-wrap (:339). MapVisitBlock has to reproduce that placement or the band animates as one unit instead of two.
known_gaps: ONE CLASS TOKEN IS LOST AND IT IS DELIBERATE. The template writes <span class="eyebrow light"> on this charcoal band (:292); MapVisitBlock follows the house rule every other block follows and emits `light` only on the sage-pale and sage bands, so /contact/ ships class="eyebrow" here. Nothing moves visually: `light` is inert under the current cascade — .contact .location-copy .eyebrow (0,3,0) at contact.css:274-277 already sets --vs-eyebrow-on-sage and beats .eyebrow.light (0,2,0) at contact.css:47 — and the block owns the charcoal eyebrow colour in its own scoped CSS. Recorded here rather than left for the class-level diff to find, because a section-class diff is exactly what this phase measures.

blocks.band_evidence: contact/index.astro:360 <section class="section"> — bare, no modifier. contact.css:160 gives .contact .section padding only and no background, so this band is the page ground, which is global.css:25 body { background-color: var(--vs-paper) } = tokens.css:12 #ffffff. FaqBlock's `paper` maps to no modifier class (BAND_CLASS), so it emits the same bare class="section".
blocks.body_not_pull_note: sections.faq.body -> `body`, NOT -> `pull`. The template puts the paragraph inside the centred .section-head (contact/index.astro:365) and this page has no .pull column at all — contact.css defines no such rule. Writing it to `pull` would move the paragraph beside the questions; writing it to both would print it twice.
blocks.no_cta_note: cta_label and cta_href are unset, and blank is correct: contact/index.astro:360-378 has no .cta-row at all. FaqBlock draws the CTA only when ctaLabel is a non-empty string, so the band ends at the accordion exactly as it does today.

literal.question: Are you accepting new patients?
literal.answer: Yes — Vivid Smiles is welcoming new patients, both locally and from out of state. Many of our smile-design and implant patients travel in from across Colorado and beyond. Request a visit through any of the contact methods on this page and our front desk will reach out within one business day.

literal.question: Where do I park?
literal.answer: There is free, on-site parking directly in front of the building at 17167 Cedar Gulch Pkwy, Suite 102. Accessible spaces are nearest the entrance. Our suite is on the ground floor — no stairs.

literal.question: Do you take my insurance?
literal.answer: We're in-network with most major PPO plans and we file claims on your behalf. We also offer an in-house dental membership plan for patients without insurance. Send your plan details through the form and our team will verify benefits before your visit.

literal.question: How quickly will you reply to my message?
literal.answer: We aim to reply to every message within one business day. Calls during office hours reach our front desk live; voicemails left after hours are returned the next morning.

literal.question: What if I have a dental emergency?
literal.answer: Please call {phone} first — same-day care is available for active pain, dental injuries, and trauma. See our emergency dentistry page for what counts as urgent and what to do before you arrive.

literal.question: What should I bring to my first visit?
literal.answer: A photo ID, your insurance card if you have one, and a list of any medications you take. Our new-patients page has the full first-visit guide, including what to expect during the consultation.

items.from_template: contact/index.astro:87-113 — the `faqs` array in the frontmatter, transcribed in order. /contact/ has NO `faqs` repeater in WordPress (pageFields.faqs is null on the live endpoint, verified 2026-08-29), so there is nothing to move and these six are the second kind of value this file allows: template copy, transcribed verbatim, with the line named.
items.open_note: Only row 1 carries `open`. It is a true_false whose default is 0, so the five rows without it save closed, which is what open={undefined} renders today.
items.phone_tokens_note: Row 5 stores {phone_href} and {phone} where the template interpolates ${phoneHref} and ${phoneLabel} (:107). The number is site data (src/data/contact.ts) and a tel: URL in a field is a phone number with a second home — the href policy. src/blocks/site-tokens.ts fills both before FaqBlock set:html's the answer, and an unknown token passes through untouched.
items.html_in_answers_is_load_bearing_here: Rows 5 and 6 carry <a> anchors — to /emergency-dentistry/ and /new-patients/ — and row 5 also carries the phone link. FaqBlock renders answers with set:html, exactly as contact/index.astro:363 does, so the links survive. Checked for the escaping trap: no answer contains a bare & or an entity, so nothing double-escapes.

_: Every repeater row on this page that no block above claims. The backfill fails, before writing

sections.reason: Its band stays in the template, unguarded — see the #reach note above. Unlike a code_section exemption, NOTHING FREEZES: contact/index.astro:260-262 still renders section("reach").eyebrow / .heading / .body on both branches, so the eyebrow, heading and body in this row keep reaching the page after the backfill exactly as they do now.
read_this_before_running: This row is exempt because its band is not migrating, not because its copy is being given up.
If #reach is ever migrated, delete this entry in the same change — an exemption that outlives
its reason is how an unclaimed row stops being noticed.

known_gaps: NOTHING ON THIS ROUTE FREEZES. Both blocks map their eyebrow/heading/body from live `sections`
rows and the exempt band keeps reading its own, so every editable word on /contact/ is still
editable after the backfill. That is the whole reason #visit is a `map_visit` layout and not a
`code_section`: the escape hatch is for bands whose copy is already in code, and five of this
page's values are not.
THE SIX FAQ ITEMS CHANGE HANDS, WHICH IS A GAIN AND A NEW DEPENDENCY. They are template copy
today and become editable rows in wp-admin after this runs. The page's FAQPage JSON-LD therefore
had to be rebuilt from the block's `items` (contact/index.astro:115-166): left pointing at the
template array it would keep describing the pre-migration questions the first moment anyone
edited one, silently, because structured data is invisible on the page. FaqBlock's own header
says the same — structured data lives on the page, so it cannot move into the band.
ONE PIECE OF DEBT IN THAT REBUILD. The JSON-LD fills {phone} / {phone_href} with two inline
String.split().join() calls instead of importing fillSiteTokens from src/blocks/site-tokens.ts,
because that file is created in a sibling Wave-B commit and a static import of a file that does
not exist yet fails `astro check` and every concurrent build — the same ordering rule that keeps
three CodeSectionBlock entries commented out. Switch the page to fillSiteTokens once
src/blocks/site-tokens.ts has landed; the substitution is duplicated until then.
THE FAQPage SCRIPT IS UNCONDITIONAL, as it is on all fifteen migrated routes. An editor who
deletes the FAQ band leaves an empty `mainEntity` behind. Not fixed here: wrapping the <script>
in a guard adds whitespace text nodes on BOTH branches and this route's else-branch is verified
byte-for-byte, so the fix belongs in a change that re-measures every FAQ route at once.
#visit LOSES ONE `light` CLASS TOKEN FROM ITS EYEBROW — colour unchanged, block-owned. The
reasoning is on the block itself under `known_gaps`.
